item.title: Djokovic wins seventh Beijing title and 102nd career crown as injured de Minaur retires
item.dc:creator: Tennis Majors and partners
item.description: Novak Djokovic (No. 6) won his seventh China Open title on Tuesday when Alex de Minaur (No. 5) retired injured with the Serb leading 7-6 (3), 0-1. At 39, Djokovic is 34-0 in Beijing and has won a title in 21 consecutive seasons. It is the 102nd crown of his career.
item.content:encoded:
Serb Novak Djokovic, the No. 6 seed, won the China Open on Tuesday afternoon when Australian Alex de Minaur, the No. 5 seed, retired injured. Djokovic had taken a tight first set 7-6 (3) and trailed 1-0 in the second when de Minaur stopped with an apparent groin injury. The 39-year-old lifted a record seventh Beijing trophy and remains unbeaten at the event, now 34-0. It is the 102nd Tour…

item.title: “What a journey since I got injured”: Alcaraz defends Tokyo title against Lehecka for first trophy since injury
item.dc:creator: Tennis Majors and partners
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz (No. 1) beat Jiri Lehecka 7-6 (4), 6-4 on Tuesday to retain his Tokyo title, his first trophy since returning from injury. At 23, the Spaniard now has 27 career titles and 10 at ATP 500 level, and he said Shanghai, Paris, the ATP Finals and the Davis Cup are next on his list.
item.content:encoded:
Spaniard Carlos Alcaraz, the top seed, beat Czech Jiri Lehecka 7-6 (4), 6-4 on Tuesday to win the Tokyo ATP 500 for the second year in a row. It is his first title in seven and a half months, after the Australian Open and Doha, and his first since returning from a five-month injury layoff. “Thinking about everything I’ve done to get here and all the hard work I’ve put in for this moment…

item.title: Sinner ends 2026 season due to knee inflammation, misses ATP Finals
item.dc:creator: Cédric Rouquette
item.description: Jannik Sinner's 2026 season is over: the Italian will undergo treatment for inflammation in his knee and will miss the ATP Finals in Turin, where he had won the last two editions. "I need to think about my long-term career," he said, promising to come back at a hundred percent.
item.content:encoded:
Jannik Sinner will not play again this year. His management team announced on Tuesday that the Italian will undergo treatment for inflammation in his knee, on the advice of his medical team, and that his 2026 season is over. “The decision has been made to have the treatment now to give Jannik the necessary time to recover before beginning preparations for 2027,” the statement…

item.title: October 6, 1986: The day Pat Cash clashed with Brad Gilbert en route to Davis Cup glory
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Sokolowski
item.description: Every day, Tennis Majors looks back to the biggest moments in tennis history. On October 6, 1986, the Australian had a falling-out with Brad Gilbert in a Davis Cup semi-final
item.content:encoded:
On this day, October 6, 1986, Pat Cash, from Australia, defeated Brad Gilbert, from the United States (3-6, 6-2, 6-3, 6-4), thus propelling the Aussie team into the Davis Cup final. An argument erupted between the two players, Gilbert accusing Cash of stalling by taking too much time to get into the return position. The Australian team would go on to win the 1986 Davis Cup, Cash being the hero of…

item.title: Djokovic into Beijing final vs. De Minaur after Medvedev is disqualified!
item.dc:creator: Tennis Majors and partners
item.description: Novak Djokovic (No. 6) reached the China Open final on Monday when Daniil Medvedev (No. 3) was disqualified with the Serb serving for the match. Djokovic, himself disqualified at the 2020 US Open, said he felt sorry for his opponent. At 39, he will face Alex de Minaur (No. 5) for the title.

Daniil Medvedev, the No. 3 seed, was disqualified with Djokovic leading 7-5, 5-3 and serving for the match. The incident came in the middle of a rally. item.title: Alcaraz recovers from a set down against Munar to set up Tokyo final with Lehecka
item.dc:creator: Tennis Majors and partners
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz (No. 1) lost the first set to Jaume Munar before winning 5-7, 6-3, 6-1 on Monday night to reach the Tokyo final for the second straight year. The defending champion said he had switched to a more aggressive game to turn the match around. He will face Jiri Lehecka for the title.
item.content:encoded:
Top seed Carlos Alcaraz lost the first set and struggled through half of the second before taking control. He beat fellow Spaniard Jaume Munar, a qualifier, 5-7, 6-3, 6-1 on Monday night to reach the final of the Tokyo ATP 500. The defending champion is into the Tokyo final for the second year in a row. It is his first final since he missed five months through injury, and his first since…

item.title: October 5, 1918: The day French aviator Roland Garros was killed during World War I
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Sokolowski
item.description: Every day Tennis Majors takes you back in time to celebrate a great moment in tennis history. Today, we go back to 1918, when Roland Garros, after whom the French Open venue was famously named, was shot down
item.content:encoded:
On this day, October 5, 1918, the famous French aviator Roland Garros, the first man to have flown over the Mediterranean Sea, was killed in the Ardennes after his plane had been shot down by the German army. Although Garros himself didn’t really play tennis, 10 years after his death, the brand new stadium built to host the Davis Cup as well as the French Championships would be named after him by…

item.title: Vintage Djokovic wins high-intensity battle with Zverev to go 32-0 in Beijing
item.dc:creator: Tennis Majors and partners
item.description: Novak Djokovic (No. 6) came from a set down to beat top seed Alexander Zverev (No. 1) 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 on Sunday and reach the China Open semifinals. At 39, he is now 32-0 in Beijing, an outright record start at a single event that moves him past Rafael Nadal. He also clashed with the umpire over a replayed point.
item.content:encoded:
Serb Novak Djokovic, the No. 6 seed, came from a set down to beat top seed Alexander Zverev 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 in two hours and 34 minutes on Sunday. The win sent him into the semifinals of the China Open and gave him an outright record. Djokovic will face Daniil Medvedev, the No. 3 seed, in the semifinals. The six-time champion is now 32-0 in Beijing. That is the longest winning streak any player…

item.dc:creator: Alexandre Sokolowski
item.description: Every day Tennis Majors looks back to the biggest moments in tennis history. On October 4, 2007, Stefan Koubek lost his temper and got disqualified against Sébastien Grosjean in Metz

On this day, October 4, 2007, Stefan Koubek, from Austria, was disqualified from the Metz Open. The left-hander, known for his ill-temper, lost his cool after a disagreement with the umpire, despite the fact that he was leading 4-2 in the deciding set of his round of 16 clash against Frenchman Sebastien Grosjean. Stefan Koubek, a left-hander with a two-handed backhand…

item.title: Alcaraz into Tokyo semifinals after injured Shapovalov retires
item.dc:creator: Tennis Majors and partners
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz (No. 1) reached the Tokyo semifinals on Sunday when Denis Shapovalov retired injured with the Spaniard leading 7-6 (3), 2-1.
item.content:encoded:
Spaniard Carlos Alcaraz, the top seed, reached the semifinals of the Tokyo ATP 500 on Sunday when Canadian Denis Shapovalov was forced to retire through injury. Alcaraz led 7-6 (3), 2-1 when Shapovalov stopped, after a chaotic tiebreak had decided an even first set. The defending champion and world No. 3 showed his sympathy afterward by signing the camera lens with a message for his…

item.title: No. 118 Charaeva stuns Rybakina in her first match as world No. 1!
item.dc:creator: Tennis Majors and partners
item.description: Alina Charaeva, ranked No. 118, came from a set down to beat Elena Rybakina (No. 1) 3-6, 6-4, 6-3 in Beijing on Saturday. She is the lowest-ranked player to come back against a world No. 1 since 1975. Rybakina becomes only the second player, after Naomi Osaka, to lose her first match at the top of the rankings.
item.content:encoded:
Elena Rybakina’s first match as world No. 1 ended in defeat. Armenian Alina Charaeva, ranked No. 118, came from a set down to beat the Kazakh top seed 3-6, 6-4, 6-3 on Saturday afternoon and reach the last 32 of the China Open. Since the WTA rankings were first published in 1975, no player ranked as low as Charaeva had ever come from behind to beat the world No. 1.

item.title: Six arguments, six answers: how a New York judge kept the PTPA case alive
item.dc:creator: Cédric Rouquette
item.category: Indian Wells BNP Paribas Open Masters 1000
The Court Report: Exclusives & Long Reads
item.description: A US District Court judge has denied all six motions to dismiss an antitrust case brought by current and former players against tennis's governing bodies. This ruling means the ATP, WTA, FFT, AELTC, and USTA must now proceed to discovery, opening their books and providing sworn evidence in a significant development for the sport's future.
item.content:encoded:
On September 30, Judge Margaret M. Garnett of the US District Court for the Southern District of New York issued a 66-page opinion in the antitrust case brought by fifteen current and former players and the Professional Tennis Players Association. The players include Vasek Pospisil, who co-founded the PTPA, Nick Kyrgios, Tennys Sandgren, Christian Harrison, Marco Trungelliti, Saisai Zheng…

item.title: What happens to betting markets when tennis stars withdraw?
item.dc:creator: Cédric Rouquette
item.description: When top tennis stars withdraw from a tournament, betting markets rapidly adjust. Oddsmakers recalculate probabilities for every remaining player, causing significant shifts in odds and liquidity. This dynamic process increases unpredictability, highlighting the complex nature of sports betting today.
item.content:encoded:
A major tennis tournament can change dramatically when its headline players withdraw. Ticket demand may soften, broadcast narratives need to be rewritten, and lesser-known competitors suddenly receive more attention. Betting markets must also adjust, often within minutes. When a top seed pulls out because of injury, illness, fatigue, or scheduling concerns, oddsmakers are not simply removing…

item.title: Sinner withdraws from Shanghai, Zverev eyes World No. 1 spot
item.dc:creator: Cédric Rouquette
item.description: Jannik Sinner withdraws from the Rolex Shanghai Masters due to his persistant knee injury, missing the Asian swing. His absence opens a significant door for Alexander Zverev to potentially claim the World No. 1 ranking, adding a dramatic twist to the ATP season.
item.content:encoded:
Jannik Sinner’s injury-hit season took another blow on Saturday when the world No. 1 officially withdrew from the 2026 Rolex Shanghai Masters, announcing on his Instagram story that his ongoing right knee problem has left him unable to play. Having already skipped the China Open in Beijing the week before, the Italian will now miss the entire Asian swing, the latest chapter in a stop-start…

item.title: Alcaraz recovers from 2-6 down in tiebreak, sweeps past Arnaldi into Tokyo quarterfinals
item.dc:creator: Tennis Majors and partners
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz (No. 1) won six straight points from 2-6 down in the first-set tiebreak and beat Matteo Arnaldi 7-6 (6), 6-1 to reach the Tokyo quarterfinals on Saturday night. The defending champion has now won seven straight matches at the event and faces Denis Shapovalov next.
item.content:encoded:
Spaniard Carlos Alcaraz, the top seed, trailed 2-6 in the first-set tiebreak against Italian Matteo Arnaldi on Saturday night. He then won six points in a row and rode the momentum to the end, beating Arnaldi 7-6 (6), 6-1 in an hour and 46 minutes to reach the quarterfinals of the Tokyo ATP 500. The defending champion and world No. 3 has now won seven straight matches in Tokyo.

item.title: October 3, 1982: The day John McEnroe sealed a place in the Davis Cup final, after an endless journey and plane scare
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Sokolowski
item.description: Every day, Tennis Majors looks back to the biggest moments in tennis history. On October 3, 1982, John McEnroe led the USA to a 5-0 win over Australia in the Davis Cup semi-finals, after a week in which he had experienced a plane scare
item.content:encoded:
On this day, October 3, 1982, John McEnroe sealed a 5-0 win for the United States against Australia in the Davis Cup semi-finals, in Perth. In the last match, McEnroe defeated John Alexander (6-4, 6-3). In fact, “Mac” and his doubles partner Peter Fleming actually experienced more difficulty travelling to Australia, surviving an plane scare and considerable delay, than winning their matches.

item.title: “It’s not stamina, it’s something else, related to health”: Djokovic on the enigma behind his 2026 form
item.dc:creator: Cédric Rouquette
item.description: After a second medical timeout in two matches in Beijing, Novak Djokovic ruled out the explanation everyone has been using for his season: "It's not stamina. It's something else. More related to health." He won't say what it is, and still plans to play Paris and, if he qualifies, Turin.
item.content:encoded:
Novak Djokovic won again in Beijing, and spent the press conference afterward explaining why winning has stopped being the hard part. The 39-year-old beat China’s Bu Yunchaokete 4-6, 7-6 (2), 6-2 on Friday to stay unbeaten in the Chinese capital at 31-0 and reach the China Open quarterfinals, but needed a medical timeout to do it, his second in two matches at the tournament.

item.title: “Excited to start a new chapter”: Auger-Aliassime hires Federer’s former coach Ljubicic, who keeps his French federation role
item.dc:creator: Cédric Rouquette
item.description: Felix Auger-Aliassime hires Ivan Ljubicic, Roger Federer's former coach, for a new chapter after a post-Wimbledon slump. Ljubicic retains his French federation advisory role, confirmed compatible with his new coaching duties.
item.content:encoded:
Felix Auger-Aliassime has a new coach, and it is Roger Federer’s last one. The world No. 5 announced on Instagram on Friday that he has started working with Ivan Ljubicic, ending a search that began when he split with Frederic Fontang after Wimbledon. “Excited to start a new chapter with Ivan. Let’s get to work,” the Canadian wrote. The pair have already begun working together in Monte-Carlo.

item.title: Djokovic fights back against Bu to match Nadal’s 31-0 record
item.dc:creator: Tennis Majors and partners
item.description: Novak Djokovic (No. 6) came from a set down to beat Yunchaokete Bu 4-6, 7-6 (2), 6-2 on Friday and reach the China Open quarterfinals. The win takes his record in Beijing to 31-0, equaling Rafael Nadal's best start at Roland-Garros.
item.content:encoded:
Serb Novak Djokovic, the No. 6 seed, lost the first set and needed almost three hours to beat Chinese wild card Yunchaokete Bu 4-6, 7-6 (2), 6-2 on Friday and reach the China Open quarterfinals. With the win, he kept his perfect record in Beijing intact. The six-time champion is now 31-0 at the event. That equals Rafael Nadal’s 31-0 start at Roland-Garros as the best opening run at a…

item.title: Fils beats Tiafoe in rare Top 10 clash as Jacquet, Vacherot and Munar complete Tokyo quarterfinals
item.dc:creator: Tennis Majors and partners
item.description: Arthur Fils (Q) beat Frances Tiafoe (No. 2) 6-3, 7-5 on Friday in Tokyo, in only the second meeting of two Top 10 players in a second round since 1992. Vacherot, Jacquet and Munar also reached the quarterfinals.
item.content:encoded:
French qualifier Arthur Fils won a rematch of the Cincinnati final on Friday, beating American Frances Tiafoe, the second seed, 6-3, 7-5 to reach the quarterfinals of the Kinoshita Group Japan Open Tennis Championships. It was only the second time since 1990 that two Top 10 players had met as early as the second round of an event, after world No. 6 Ivan Lendl beat No. 10 Goran Ivanisevic in…

item.title: Alcaraz saves three set points, then pulls away from Michelsen to stay perfect in Tokyo
item.dc:creator: Tennis Majors and partners
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz (No. 1) saved three set points and lost the second set before running away with the third to beat Alex Michelsen 7-6 (1), 4-6, 6-1 in Tokyo. The defending champion, now unbeaten in six matches at the event, said the slow conditions had stopped him playing his aggressive game.
item.content:encoded:

He then ran away with the decider to beat American Alex Michelsen 7-6 (1), 4-6, 6-1 on Thursday and reach the second round of the Kinoshita Group Japan Open Tennis Championships.
